card.statement:
Consider representation-tame non-primitive critical poset
$\mathcal P=(N,4)$, which has the following Hasse quiver
\begin{center}
$\xymatrix @-1pc
            {&&{\circ}\ar@{->}[r]&{\circ}\ar@{->}[dr]\\
             &&{\circ}\ar@{->}[r]\ar@{->}[ur]&{\circ}\ar@{->}[r]&{*}\\
                {\circ}\ar@{->}[r]&{\circ}\ar@{->}[r]&{\circ}\ar@{->}[r]&{\circ}\ar@{->}[ur]}$
\end{center}
Fix the dimension vector $d_{(N,4)}=(5;2,4,3,2;1,2,3,4)$. One
can check that with respect to the weight
$\chi=(5;2,1,1,2;1,1,1,1)$ there exists at least one stable
representation in dimension $d_{(N,4)}$, hence the corresponding GIT quotient is
not empty. Due to the dimension formula we have at least
$1-\langle d_{\mathcal P},d_{\mathcal P} \rangle+2\cdot5=1$--parametric family of uni-classes of representation of
$\mathcal P_\chi-usp$. Moreover, it is possible to show that this
is a maximal number of parameters. Therefore, we have that for
the weight $\chi=(5;2,1,1,2;1,1,1,1)$ the set of uni-classes of
orthoscalar representations of $\mathcal P$ in dimension
$d_{(N,4)}$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$.
card.label: Example 26

paper.title: Representations of posets: Linear versus Unitary
paper.abstract: A number of recent papers treated the representation theory of partially ordered sets in unitary spaces with the so called orthoscalar relation. Such theory generalizes the classical theory which studies the representations of partially ordered sets in linear spaces. It happens that the results in the unitary case are well-correlated with those in the linear case. The purpose of this article is to shed light on this phenomena.
